profile.name: Glenn Phillips
profile.writeup:
In a sport where places in the side are usually earned with the bat or ball, Glenn Phillips belongs to a rare breed of cricketer who can walk into a team purely on the strength of what he does in the field. His flying catches, direct-hit run-outs, and seemingly impossible reflexes have made him a highlight-reel regular across every league he's played in, and pundits and opposition players alike routinely rank him among the best fielders the game has ever seen.


Originally hailing from South Africa, Phillips moved to New Zealand at a young age and quickly rose through the ranks with his impressive batting skills and consistency. Phillips' journey began as a promising batter and reliable wicketkeeper. He made his List A debut in the Ford Trophy in January 2015, leaving an immediate impact with his aggressive style of play. Representing New Zealand in the U-19 World Cup in 2016, he emerged as the second-highest run-scorer for his team, further solidifying his status as a rising star.


In domestic cricket, Phillips made a spectacular debut for the Otago Volts in the Super Smash T20 competition with an explosive innings. His consistency throughout the tournament saw him finish as the leading run-scorer, earning him a spot in New Zealand's T20I squad. Although selected for the ODI squad against India in 2017, Phillips had to wait five years to make his 50-over debut. During this period, he continued to build his reputation as a power hitter. In 2020, he grabbed global attention with a stunning century in a T20I match against the West Indies, showcasing his ability to dismantle bowlers with ease. Earlier that year, Phillips achieved another milestone, earning his maiden Test cap during the Sydney Test.


From 2020 onwards, Glenn made a significant impact in T20 leagues around the world. It all started with a standout season for Jamaica Tallawahs in the Caribbean Premier League, followed by an impressive run with Gloucestershire in the T20 Blast. His big break came at the 2022 T20 World Cup, where he stole the spotlight with a stunning century against Sri Lanka. Phillips finished as New Zealand's highest run-scorer in the tournament, although they were knocked out in the semifinals.


Riding on the back of his consistent performances in domestic cricket, Phillips made a successful return to the Test side in 2023. Seizing the opportunity, he showcased his all-round skills in challenging conditions during New Zealand's tour of Bangladesh. During New Zealand's historic tour of India, Glenn may not have had the best series with the bat, but he made sure to contribute significantly with his off-spin. His vital role added depth to the Kiwi attack, and his all-round skills helped New Zealand pull off a remarkable 3-0 whitewash, a feat never before achieved by an away side in India.


Phillips continued to add to his growing reputation as one of the most sought-after T20 players in the world. New Zealand's strong run in white-ball cricket continued through 2025 and 2026, with the side reaching the final of the ICC Champions Trophy in 2025 and the ICC T20 World Cup in 2026, with Phillips remaining a central figure during this period. His growth as an all-format player was underlined in June 2026, when he brought up his maiden Test century against England at The Oval. In doing so, Phillips became only the third New Zealand player, after Brendon McCullum and Martin Guptill, to score international centuries in all three formats.
